about: Skills tool: Hardy-Weinberg calculations. Solver and generator: ApBioProblems, kind hw (mode counts or recessive). Built now, published with Unit 7: every item is tagged stats-hardy-weinberg, whose map entry sits after the Unit 7 topic hardy-weinberg, so the generator serves it only once Unit 7 is published.
intro: Find allele frequencies from genotype counts or from the share of individuals showing a recessive trait, and predict genotype frequencies for a population in Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium.
howItWorksTitle: The equations, their assumptions, and how answers are checked
howItWorks:
p + q = 1

p² + 2pq + q² = 1

  • p and q are the frequencies of the two alleles of one gene; p², 2pq and q² are the expected frequencies of the two homozygous genotypes and the heterozygote.
  • From genotype counts, count alleles: every individual carries two. From a recessive phenotype, q² is the share of individuals showing it, because only homozygous recessive individuals do.
  • The genotype frequencies are expected only if the population is in equilibrium: very large, mating at random, with no mutation, no migration and no natural selection.
  • Frequencies count when within one unit of the last decimal place asked for (0.01 for p, q and 2pq; 0.001 for q²) or 1%; numbers of individuals within 2%.
